title: CI gates: lint, typecheck, unit, schema-validation, freshness report, no-recipient-PII/no-tracker audit
context: The CI pipeline is the automated enforcement layer for food-assistance-maps' safety properties. Freshness, provenance completeness, and the absence of recipient PII are not just policies — they must be machine-checked on every commit so no bad entry can be published without triggering a build failure. The no-tracker audit requires defense in depth: a static grep is not sufficient; a runtime network-interception E2E is also required. Depends on food-maps-schema-001 for schema-validation integration.
objective: Implement a CI pipeline (GitHub Actions or equivalent) that runs on every PR and push: (1) lint (ESLint), (2) TypeScript typecheck, (3) unit tests (Vitest), (4) build-time JSON Schema validation of every entry in data/ against the food-assistance-maps schema, (5) a freshness report (counts of entries within/over SLA, fails if threshold not met for the pilot region), and (6) a defense-in-depth no-recipient-PII/no-tracker audit combining a static field grep AND a runtime network-interception E2E that fails on any unexpected outbound request from the directory view (CSP enforced).
acceptanceCriteria: CI runs on every PR and push to main; all gates must be green before a PR can be merged
Lint (ESLint) and TypeScript typecheck gates fail on any error
Unit tests run via Vitest; build fails on any test failure
Build-time schema validation runs ajv against every JSON entry in data/ and fails the build on any schema violation
A freshness report is generated showing count of entries within/over SLA; build fails if entries past the demote window are present in the authoritative dataset
The no-recipient-PII audit includes a static grep for PII-shaped field names (name, DOB, ssn, household, income, client_id) that fails if any such field is found in data/

The no-tracker audit includes both a static check (no tracker script URLs in the view source) AND a runtime network-interception E2E (Playwright) that fails on any unexpected outbound request from the directory view
CSP headers are enforced in the static build and verified by the E2E test
CI config is documented and the CI badge is visible in README
output: .github/workflows/ci.yml (CI pipeline definition) with all six gates implemented and passing on the pilot dataset.
